EventTitle: Birth of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Banu Hashim, Aminah bint Wahb
EventSummary: Born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant; orphaned early; raised by grandfather Abd al-Muttalib and uncle Abu Talib.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn Hisham, As-Seerah 1/158; Ibn Sa'd, At-Tabaqat 1/100

EventTitle: Inauguration of Quranic Revelation at Cave Hira
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Archangel Jibril, Khadijah bint Khuwaylid
EventSummary: Descent of the inaugural revelation (Surah Al-Alaq 96:1–5) commanding literacy, learning, and monotheism.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Sahih al-Bukhari #3; Sahih Muslim #160

EventTitle: The Hijrah (Migration to Madinah) & Start of Islamic Calendar
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, Al-Ansar, Al-Muhajirun
EventSummary: Historic migration establishing the first sovereign Islamic commonwealth; designated by Umar as year 1 AH.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: At-Tabari, Tarikh 2/368; Sahih al-Bukhari #3905

EventTitle: Constitution of Madinah (Mithaq al-Madinah)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Muslim and Jewish communities of Madinah
EventSummary: The world's first written constitutional charter establishing civic equality, religious freedom, and mutual defense.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn Hisham, As-Seerah 2/147–150; Abu Ubayd, Kitab al-Amwal

EventTitle: The Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat al-Wada') & Universal Charter
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, 124,000 Sahaba
EventSummary: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ delivered the Farewell Sermon codifying racial equality, women's rights, and sanctity of life.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Sahih Muslim #1218; Musnad Ahmad #23416

EventTitle: Passing of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ & Accession of Abu Bakr
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, Umar ibn al-Khattab
EventSummary: The Prophet ﷺ passed to the Highest Companion; Abu Bakr elected first Caliph at Saqifah; preservation of the Ummah.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Sahih al-Bukhari #4462; At-Tabari, Tarikh 3/198

EventTitle: Compilation of the Holy Quran into First Verified Volume
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, Umar ibn al-Khattab, Zayd ibn Thabit
EventSummary: Commissioned following Yamamah to gather all written manuscripts verified by two witnesses into a single Suhuf codex.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Sahih al-Bukhari #4986; Ibn Abi Dawud, Kitab al-Masahif

EventTitle: Battle of Yarmouk & Liberation of the Levant
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Khalid ibn al-Walid, Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Byzantine Army
EventSummary: Decisive strategic victory ending Byzantine rule in Syria and opening the Levant to Islamic civilization.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Al-Baladhuri, Futuh al-Buldan p. 135; At-Tabari 3/395

EventTitle: Treaty of Jerusalem (Al-Uhda al-Umariyyah)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab, Patriarch Sophronius
EventSummary: Umar personally accepted the surrender of Jerusalem, guaranteeing Christian citizens freedom of religion and property.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: At-Tabari, Tarikh 3/609; Michael the Syrian, Chronicle

EventTitle: Standardization and Distribution of the Uthmanic Mushaf
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Caliph Uthman ibn Affan, Zayd ibn Thabit, Commission of Four
EventSummary: Canonical copies of the Quranic Mushaf in the Qurayshi dialect dispatched to Kufa, Basra, Damascus, and Makkah.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Sahih al-Bukhari #4987; Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah 7/167

EventTitle: Establishment of the Umayyad Caliphate in Damascus
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Mu'awiyah I, Al-Hasan ibn Ali
EventSummary: Reconciliation ending civil division; establishment of Damascus as the administrative imperial capital.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: At-Tabari, Tarikh 5/163; Ibn al-Athir, Al-Kamil 3/201

EventTitle: Construction of the Dome of the Rock (Qubbat as-Sakhrah)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, Engineers Raja ibn Haywah & Yazid ibn Salam
EventSummary: Erection of the earliest surviving monumental Islamic architectural masterpiece featuring Quranic epigraphy.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Metropolitan Museum Timeline; K. A. C. Creswell, Early Muslim Architecture

EventTitle: Arabicization of Imperial Administration (Ta'rib ad-Diwan)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf
EventSummary: Replacement of Greek, Pahlavi, and Coptic administrative records with Arabic; minting of epigraphic Islamic dinars.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Al-Baladhuri, Futuh al-Buldan p. 193; Encyclopaedia of Islam

EventTitle: Landing of Tariq ibn Ziyad at Gibraltar (Jabal Tariq)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Tariq ibn Ziyad, Musa ibn Nusayr, Visigothic Kingdom
EventSummary: Inaugurated eight centuries of Islamic civilization in the Iberian Peninsula (Al-Andalus).
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr wal-Maghrib; Al-Maqqari, Nafh at-Tib

EventTitle: Arrival of Muhammad ibn al-Qasim in Sindh
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, Raja Dahir
EventSummary: Established early Islamic presence in South Asia, guaranteeing freedom of worship to Buddhist and Hindu subjects.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Al-Baladhuri, Futuh al-Buldan; Chachnama (tr. Mirza Kalichbeg)

EventTitle: Reign of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (Umar II)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
EventSummary: Revered as the fifth Rightly Guided Caliph; restored rigorous ethical accountability; eliminated poverty across provinces.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Sirat Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz; At-Tabari

EventTitle: The Abbasid Revolution & Fall of the Umayyads
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Abu al-Abbas as-Saffah, Abu Muslim al-Khurasani
EventSummary: Overthrow of the Umayyad dynasty; establishment of the Abbasid Caliphate emphasizing universal Islamic equity.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: At-Tabari, Tarikh 7/424; Hugh Kennedy, The Early Abbasid Caliphate

EventTitle: Consolidation of the Umayyad Emirate of Cordoba
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Abd al-Rahman I (Ad-Dakhil / The Falcon of Quraysh)
EventSummary: Established an independent, prosperous Islamic state in Iberia following escape from Abbasid overthrow.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn Hayyan, Al-Muqtabis; Al-Maqqari, Nafh at-Tib 1/210

EventTitle: Founding of Baghdad (Madinat al-Salam, City of Peace)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, Nawbakht, Mashallah
EventSummary: Construction of the celebrated circular capital of the Abbasids, developing into the intellectual capital of the world.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, Tarikh Baghdad 1/66; At-Tabari 7/614

EventTitle: Reign of Harun al-Rashid & Zenith of Bayt al-Hikmah
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Caliph Harun al-Rashid, Barmakid Viziers
EventSummary: Golden age of diplomacy (exchanges with Charlemagne), founding of the House of Wisdom, flowering of urban culture.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn an-Nadim, Al-Fihrist; Al-Mas'udi, Muruj adh-Dhahab

EventTitle: Publication of Al-Kitab al-Mukhtasar fi Hisab al-Jabr wal-Muqabala
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi
EventSummary: Inaugurated algebra as an independent mathematical discipline; introduced Hindu-Arabic numerals to global science.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Roshdi Rashed, Al-Khwarizmi: The Beginnings of Algebra; George Sarton

EventTitle: Founding of the University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Fatima al-Fihri, Idrisid Dynasty
EventSummary: Recognized by UNESCO and Guinness as the oldest continuously operating higher educational institution in the world.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn Abi Zar, Rawd al-Qirtas; UNESCO World Heritage Centre

EventTitle: Proclamation of the Caliphate of Cordoba
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Caliph Abd al-Rahman III (An-Nasir)
EventSummary: Declared Cordoba an imperial caliphate, ushering in the golden age of Andalusi culture, sciences, and architecture.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn Hayyan, Al-Muqtabis Vol. 5; E. Lévi-Provençal, Histoire de l'Espagne musulmane

EventTitle: Founding of Cairo (Al-Qahirah) and Al-Azhar Mosque
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Cairo, Egypt
EventSummary: Jawhar al-Siqilli, Caliph Al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Established Cairo as imperial capital and Al-Azhar as mosque-university, becoming the global center of Sunnite scholarship.
ReviewStatus: Al-Maqrizi, Al-Khitat 1/377; Ibn Khallikan, Wafayat al-A'yan

EventTitle: Publication of Ibn al-Haytham's Kitab al-Manazir (Book of Optics)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Al-Hasan Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen)
EventSummary: Revolutionized optics by proving light enters the eye; founded the modern empirical scientific method.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: A. I. Sabra, The Optics of Ibn al-Haytham (Warburg Institute, 1989)

EventTitle: Completion of Ibn Sina's Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb (The Canon of Medicine)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
EventSummary: The definitive 14-volume medical encyclopedia that served as the primary medical curriculum in Europe and the East for 600 years.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Encyclopaedia Iranica (Avicenna); Nancy Siraisi, Avicenna in Renaissance Italy

EventTitle: Establishment of the Nizamiyyah Academy in Baghdad
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Nizam al-Mulk (Grand Vizier), Abu Hamid al-Ghazali
EventSummary: Pioneered institutionalized higher education with salaried professors, student stipends, and structured Shariah curricula.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn al-Athir, Al-Kamil 10/52; George Makdisi, The Rise of Colleges

EventTitle: Battle of Manzikert (Malazgirt)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Sultan Alp Arslan (Great Seljuk), Emperor Romanos IV Diogenes
EventSummary: Decisive Seljuk victory breaking Byzantine frontier defenses and opening Anatolia to permanent Turkish-Islamic settlement.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn al-Athir, Al-Kamil 10/66; Carole Hillenbrand, Turkish Myth and Muslim Symbol

EventTitle: Battle of Hattin & Chivalric Recovery of Jerusalem
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Sultan Salahuddin al-Ayyubi (Saladin), Balian of Ibelin
EventSummary: Salahuddin crushed Crusader field army at Hattin and liberated Jerusalem, extending universal pardon and ransom leniency.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Baha al-Din ibn Shaddad, Al-Nawadir al-Sultaniyyah; Ibn al-Athir

EventTitle: Founding of the Delhi Sultanate
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Qutb al-Din Aibak, Mamluk (Slave) Dynasty of Delhi
EventSummary: Established permanent Islamic sovereign rule in Northern India; commissioned the Qutb Minar and Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Minhaj-i-Siraj Juzjani, Tabaqat-i-Nasiri; K. A. Nizami, Delhi Sultanat

EventTitle: Catastrophic Sack of Baghdad by the Mongols
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Hulagu Khan, Caliph Al-Musta'sim Billah
EventSummary: Destruction of the historical Abbasid caliphal capital, House of Wisdom, and mass destruction of manuscript archives.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah 13/200; Rashid al-Din, Jami' al-Tawarikh

EventTitle: Battle of Ayn Jalut & Halting of the Mongol Invasions
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Sultan Sayf ad-Din Qutuz, Emir Baybars, Kitbuqa Noyan
EventSummary: Decisive Mamluk victory destroying Mongol army, permanently saving Syria, Egypt, and North Africa from destruction.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn Taghribirdi, Al-Nujum az-Zahirah 7/84; Al-Maqrizi, Al-Suluk

EventTitle: Founding of the Ottoman Principality in Bithynia
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Osman I (Osman Gazi)
EventSummary: Inception of the Ottoman state from a frontier border principality (Uç Beyliği), growing into a 6-century cross-continental empire.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Halil Inalcik, The Ottoman Empire; Cemal Kafadar, Between Two Worlds

EventTitle: Conversion of the Ilkhanate to Islam under Ghazan Khan
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Sultan Mahmud Ghazan Khan, Vizier Rashid al-Din
EventSummary: The Mongol rulers of Persia embraced Sunnite Islam, inaugurating a golden age of Persianate art, architecture, and historical chronicles.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Rashid al-Din, Jami' al-Tawarikh; Charles Melville, The Fall of Amir Chupan

EventTitle: Celebrated Trans-Saharan Hajj Pilgrimage of Mansa Musa
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Mansa Musa (Emperor of Mali), Sultan Al-Nasir Muhammad
EventSummary: Musa traveled with 60,000 attendants and 12,000 servants carrying pure gold, elevating Mali and Timbuktu to global renown.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Al-Umari, Masalik al-Absar; Ibn Battuta; Nehemia Levtzion

EventTitle: Voyages of Ibn Battuta across the Islamic World
GeographicLocation: Across 73,000 miles (Africa, Levant, Persia, India, SE Asia, China)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Ibn Battuta (Shaykh of Tangier), Sultan Abu Inan of Fez
EventSummary: Traveled three times farther than Marco Polo, documenting institutions, societies, and commercial connectivity of the Dar al-Islam.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ibn Battuta, Tuhfat an-Nuzzar; tr. H. A. R. Gibb (Hakluyt Society)

EventTitle: Founding of the Malacca Sultanate
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Parameswara (Sultan Iskandar Shah)
EventSummary: Became the supreme trading entrepôt and spiritual engine for the peaceful spread of Islam throughout Southeast Asia.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Sejarah Melayu (Malay Annals); Tome Pires, Suma Oriental

EventTitle: Maritime Expeditions of Admiral Zheng He
GeographicLocation: Indian Ocean, SE Asia, South Asia, Arabia, Swahili Coast
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Admiral Zheng He (Hajji Mahmud Shams), Ming Yongle Emperor
EventSummary: Chinese Muslim admiral commanded colossal treasure fleets of 300 ships, fostering commercial ties with Islamic sultanates.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ma Huan, Yingya Shenglan (The Overall Survey of the Ocean's Shores)

EventTitle: Conquest of Constantinople (Fath al-Qustantiniyyah)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Sultan Mehmed II Al-Fatih, Emperor Constantine XI
EventSummary: Twenty-one-year-old Sultan conquered the Byzantine capital, fulfilling Prophetic glad tidings and transforming Istanbul into an Islamic capital.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Musnad Ahmad #18977; Tursun Beg, Tarikh-i Abu'l Fath; Franz Babinger

EventTitle: Fall of Granada & End of Islamic Sovereign Rule in Iberia
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Sultan Muhammad XII (Boabdil), Ferdinand and Isabella
EventSummary: Surrender of the Nasrid Kingdom of Granada following an 8-month siege; subsequent violation of capitulation treaties and expulsion of Moriscos.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Al-Maqqari, Nafh at-Tib; L. P. Harvey, Islamic Spain 1250 to 1500

EventTitle: Establishment of the Safavid Empire in Iran
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Shah Ismail I Safavi
EventSummary: Unified Persia under imperial rule, establishing Ithna Ashari Shi'ism as state religion and fostering exquisite Persianate arts.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Encyclopaedia Iranica (Safavids); Roger Savory, Iran under the Safavids

EventTitle: Ottoman Conquest of Cairo & Transfer of Caliphal Relics
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Sultan Selim I (Yavuz), Caliph Al-Mutawakkil III
EventSummary: Defeated Mamluks at Marj Dabiq and Raydaniyyah; established Ottoman custody over Makkah, Madinah, and Jerusalem.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Halil Inalcik, The Ottoman Empire; Caroline Finkel, Osman's Dream

EventTitle: Battle of Panipat & Foundation of the Mughal Empire
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Zahir al-Din Muhammad Babur, Sultan Ibrahim Lodi
EventSummary: Babur's field artillery defeated Lodi forces, establishing the Mughal Empire which commanded 25% of global GDP at its peak.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Babur, Baburnama (tr. Thackston); Ferishta; Ebba Koch, Mughal Architecture

EventTitle: Reign of Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent (Al-Qanuni)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Sultan Suleiman I, Grand Mufti Ebusuud Efendi, Mimar Sinan
EventSummary: Zenith of Ottoman statecraft, synthesis of Hanafi jurisprudence with secular statutory law (Qanun), building of Süleymaniye Mosque.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Halil Inalcik; Colin Imber, Ebusu'ud: The Islamic Legal Tradition

EventTitle: Compilation of the Fatawa-e-Alamgiri
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Emperor Aurangzeb Alamgir, Commission of 500 Jurists led by Shaykh Nizam
EventSummary: Most comprehensive codification of Hanafi Shariah jurisprudence in South Asian history, serving as official law of the empire.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Fatawa-e-Alamgiri (Al-Fatawa al-Hindiyyah, 6 vols); Muhammad Saqi Musta'id Khan

EventTitle: Intellectual Revival & Hadith Reform of Shah Waliullah Dehlawi
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Shah Waliullah al-Dehlawi
EventSummary: Pioneered Persian translation of the Quran, reconciled divergent Sunnite jurisprudence, authored Hujjat Allah al-Balighah.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Shah Waliullah, Hujjat Allah al-Balighah; J. M. S. Baljon, Religion and Thought of Shah Wali Allah

EventTitle: The Tanzimat Legal & Administrative Modernization Reforms
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Sultan Abdulmejid I, Mustafa Reshid Pasha, Midhat Pasha
EventSummary: Edict of Gülhane (1839) and Imperial Reform Edict (1856) guaranteeing civil equality, drafting the Mecelle civil code.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Halil Inalcik; Stanford Shaw, History of the Ottoman Empire

EventTitle: The 1857 Indian Uprising & Dissolution of the Mughal Empire
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar, British East India Company
EventSummary: Massive anti-colonial uprising ending in direct British crown rule (Raj) and the exile of the final Mughal emperor.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: William Dalrymple, The Last Mughal; Ayesha Jalal

EventTitle: Pan-Islamic Reform Movement of Jamal al-Din al-Afghani & Muhammad Abduh
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Jamal al-Din al-Afghani, Muhammad Abduh, Rashid Rida
EventSummary: Advocated anti-imperial solidarity, intellectual rejuvenation, scientific education, and reopening the gates of Ijtihad.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Albert Hourani, Arabic Thought in the Liberal Age 1798–1939

EventTitle: Dissolution of the Ottoman Caliphate
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, Grand National Assembly of Turkey
EventSummary: Abolition of the Ottoman Sultanate (1922) and Caliphate (1924), concluding 13 centuries of continuous caliphal institution.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Bernard Lewis, The Emergence of Modern Turkey; Erik-Jan Zürcher

EventTitle: Publication of Allama Iqbal's Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Allama Muhammad Iqbal
EventSummary: Philosophical masterpiece articulating dynamic Islamic spiritual revival, ijtihad, and moral sovereignty in the modern world.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Muhammad Iqbal, The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam (Oxford, 1934)

EventTitle: Emergence of the Sovereign Muslim State of Pakistan
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Muhammad Ali Jinnah (Quaid-e-Azam), Allama Iqbal, Muslim League
EventSummary: First modern nation-state explicitly created in the name of Islamic political self-determination for South Asian Muslims.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Ian Talbot, Pakistan: A Modern History; Ayesha Jalal, The Sole Spokesman

EventTitle: Establishment of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Leaders of 25 founding Muslim sovereign states
EventSummary: Creation of the second largest intergovernmental organization after the UN, uniting 57 member states across four continents.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: OIC Official Charter; John L. Esposito, The Islamic World: Past and Present

EventTitle: Global Ummah in the 21st Century & Digital Democratization
KeyFiguresAndInstitutions: Scholars, Universities, Educational Portals, Global Islamic Economy
EventSummary: Growth of ethical Islamic finance ($4+ trillion), international humanitarian networks, democratization of authentic knowledge.
PrimaryAndSecondarySources: Pew Research Center (Future of World Religions); State of the Global Islamic Economy Report
